Prestigious

press-TIJ-us — stress the TIJ; a prestigious prize always gets good press. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Prestigious is admired and respected as one of the very best of its kind.

She was accepted into a prestigious university known around the world.

Worked Example

Scientists spend their whole careers dreaming of one particular medal. Winning it instantly makes international headlines, and past recipients include the most celebrated researchers in history. Universities proudly list even a single winner on their websites for decades.

An honor that commands that level of respect and admiration is prestigious. Unlike 'popular,' which means widely liked, prestigious means carrying high status and earning deep respect.

How Prestigious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

acclaimed

acclaimed: publicly praised and celebrated

distinguished

distinguished: marked by excellence and honor

respected

respected: held in high regard

Antonyms

disreputable

disreputable: having a bad reputation

humble

humble: ordinary and low in status

How Strong Is It? — reputable → prestigious → legendary

reputable vs. prestigious

reputable vs. prestigious: Reputable is weaker than prestigious — a reputable school is simply trustworthy and decent, while a prestigious one commands top-tier admiration.

legendary vs. prestigious

legendary vs. prestigious: Legendary is stronger than prestigious: a legendary award is so admired that its fame has become the stuff of stories.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — prestig

Root — prestig: dazzling illusion, conjurer's trick (from Latin praestigiae, a juggler's tricks)

Suffix — -ious

Suffix — -ious: full of (Latin -osus)

Put it together

Put it together: Prestig ('dazzling illusion, conjurer's trick' — from Latin praestigiae, a juggler's dazzling tricks) + -ious ('full of'): prestigious originally meant 'full of illusion.' Over time the 'dazzle' shifted from trickery to reputation — something so admired it dazzles us.

Use the root in a new word: prestige

Use the root in a new word: prestige: Winning the state championship brought great prestige to the small school.
